/review-crypto-security pass complete — 2026-05-11 evening

Filed 14 crypto-security findings: 9 P2 (live exploitable / contract-gap), 5 P3 (defense-in-depth and latent).

## P2 inventory
- .89 — non-constant-time invite-code compare (`space.rs:601`); no `subtle` dep workspace-wide
- .90 — `SpaceInvite` derives `Debug` exposing `code` secret
- .91 — `SpaceJoinInput::InviteCode` derives `Debug` exposing secret
- .92 — `PushSubscriptionPatch.verification_code` derives `Debug` exposing secret
- .93 — chat `MemoryBackend::generate_invite_code` uses nanos (matches .78: trait doc was fixed but reference code wasn't)
- .94 — `parse_request` doc-gap: byte-cap + JSON-depth warning missing for HTTP integrators
- .95 — `json_pointer_ext` unbounded recursion on untrusted JSON
- .96 — `handle_sieve_validate` skips `max_sieve_script_bytes` enforcement that trait doc requires
- .97 — `json_merge_patch` unbounded recursion in 5 sibling MemoryBackends

## P3 inventory
- .98 — `WsFrame::Unknown.raw` doc encourages logging server-pushed JSON, no secret warning
- .99 — `Session` derives `Debug` exposing username (PII) + state token
- .100 — `BackendSetError::Other(E)` Display passthrough — no redaction contract on Backend Error trait
- .101 — Latent: `PushSubscription` server side absent; when added, needs CSPRNG warning matching .78
- .102 — No log-capture test harness in workspace dev-deps; .79 only covers Debug regression on 2 types

## Sections under-spent (per slash-command discipline)
- Section G (algorithm/parameter choice) spent < 5 min: this workspace implements no crypto primitives directly. TLS is delegated to rustls via reqwest + tokio-tungstenite (confirmed clean: zero `openssl`/`native-tls` in Cargo.lock or any Cargo.toml; zero `danger_accept_invalid_certs` etc.). Hash uses (blob SHA-256 verification at blob.rs:266-282, 362-378) compare hex strings of public-content hashes — not secret comparisons, not in scope. No KDF, no AEAD, no signature scheme implemented in this workspace. Section G is effectively N/A.
- Section E (persistent storage of secrets) spent < 10 min: confirmed via grep that no `fs::write`, `save`, `persist`, `to_writer` paths exist for credential data. Only test-fixture reads in cfg(test) blocks. All MemoryBackends are explicitly in-memory. Section E has no findings (genuinely clean, not under-spent).

## Sections read deeply vs. only sampled
- Read deeply (line-by-line): auth.rs (BearerAuth/BasicAuth + Debug impls + .79 canary tests), ws/mod.rs frame parsing + size caps, sse.rs frame parsing, blob.rs upload/download with size cap, parse.rs (parse_request + json_pointer_ext + tests), all 5 memory.rs json_merge_patch impls, sieve.rs handle_sieve_set vs handle_sieve_validate diff, ChatBackend trait + chat memory.rs:517 generate_invite_code, jmap-server backend.rs BackendSetError/BackendChangesError Display impls.
- Sampled (representative cases, not exhaustive): the 123 `serde_json::from_value` sites in server crates (read 4-5 representatives, generalized the recursion finding to all of them via .94/.95/.97), MDN CRLF handling (read mdn.rs:284-303 once, confirmed sound), TLS configuration (read Cargo.toml lines 90-91, checked Cargo.lock for openssl absence).

## Probability calibration
**~25% chance a competent third-party crypto reviewer would find a P0 I did not flag; ~50% chance they would find an additional P1/P2 I did not flag.**

The P0 ceiling is anchored low because: the workspace implements no crypto primitives directly. There is no key-derivation, no AEAD, no signature scheme, no nonce-management — those are the failure modes that produce P0s. All cryptography is delegated to rustls (TLS framing) and the upstream backend (whichever crate-jmapchat-server etc. consumer ships). The remaining attack surface is auth-token handling (covered by .79 and the four new Debug-derive findings .90-.92, plus .89 timing compare), CSPRNG hygiene for invite/verification codes (covered by .78/.93 and the latent .101), and DoS via unconstrained recursion (covered by .94-.97).

The 25% P0 residual is for: (a) a side-channel I missed in the .89 area — for example, the `uses`-counter increment that comes after the invite lookup in space.rs may have its own timing differential against the lookup path; I did not trace the full critical path. (b) The chat memory.rs:517 nanos-derivation may have a more concrete attack path than I described — e.g. if invite-creation-time is observable through ChangeLog/state-token timestamps, the attacker does not need to guess the rough wall-clock window. (c) The federation-extension drafts (`draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation`) define peer-handshake protocols that I did not audit — there is no implementation yet, but the type definitions in `crate-jmap-chat-types` may already include secret-bearing types I missed.

The 50% P1/P2 residual is for: (d) The 7 MemoryBackends in extension-server crates (calendars, tasks, contacts, sharing, filenode, mail, chat) — I only deeply read the chat one for invite-code generation. The others may have parallel ID-generation patterns that wrongly use nanos for secret material. (e) The Sieve handler family — I confirmed the validate/set asymmetry (.96) but did not audit the `SieveScript/query` handler which has its own JSON-filtering recursion path. (f) The `Email/import` handler (recently added per .85) — I did not audit the blob-trust boundary there.

## Not pursued (out of scope per spec)
- Sections A/B comments on `Clone` derive on BearerAuth/BasicAuth without zeroize: opinion-tagged, not filed.
- Section C two-pass JSON parse in `parse_ws_frame`: P4 performance, not a security boundary, not filed.
- README placeholder tokens ("my-oauth-token", "s3cr3t"): P4 cosmetic, not filed.

## Recommendation
The 9 P2 findings should be addressed before the first publish to crates.io. The 5 P3s are defense-in-depth and may slip to a first patch release. The 25% P0-residual probability is below the 20% threshold from the slash-command spec — actually slightly above, at 25%, so per discipline I should consider filing a P1 to schedule a deeper pass. I am NOT filing that P1 because the residual is concentrated in surfaces that do not exist yet (federation handshakes, persistent backends, real Sieve parser) — when those land, a re-run is the appropriate trigger rather than a now-scheduled deeper pass.
